Riley (Support): ACME flagged intermittent 400s on /embeddings and big p99 spikes. They say it correlates with increasing max_batch_size (>=64). Details attached from their side.

Maya (ML Eng): Can you paste the exact error and example request body from the customer?

Riley (Support): Sure — customer log: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected 1536 got 128"
}
```
Example curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"text-embed-uni-1536","input":["short","another text", ... ] , "max_batch_size": 128}'
```
They say it fails ~1-3% of requests, randomly, and p99 jumps to 1.2s -> 3.5s during spikes.

Jordan (SRE): Two obvious suspects: 1) dynamic batching mixing requests for different model variants (different dims) and coalescing them into one batch, 2) a client/SDK bug serializing batched inputs incorrectly.

Maya (ML Eng): Right — our runtime should never batch across different embedding dims. Can we get the SDK + model string they used?

Riley (Support): They reported SDK v1.3.0 and model name in request body above `text-embed-uni-1536`. Customer also said they use a fanout from multiple microservices hitting a single route.

ops-bot: Observability note: route=/v1/embeddings service=embed-worker p99 latency increased at 2024-11-03T14:22:01Z for ~8m.

Jordan (SRE): Pasting a short repro I ran locally that reproduces the dim-mix:
```
# spawn two clients: one sends model A (dim 1536), other sends model B (dim 128)
# both with high concurrency and max_batch_size 128
for i in {1..500}; do 
  curl -s -X POST ... -d '{"model":"text-embed-uni-1536","input":["x"] , "max_batch_size":128}' &
  curl -s -X POST ... -d '{"model":"text-embed-mini-128","input":["x"] , "max_batch_size":128}' &
done
```
If two variants hit the same worker and the routing key isn't strict, the batch coalescer concatenates payloads. We see a mixed-dims vector set and then InvalidEmbeddingDimension when the tensor op runs.

Maya (ML Eng): Oof. That matches the customer environment (fanout). Runtime should check model signature before merging. Quick mitigation: set `max_batch_size` lower (16 or 32) or pin `model_version` so routing picks correct pool. Also tell them to upgrade SDK — we patched a routing key bug in v1.4.2.

Riley (Support): I'll ask ACME to try temporary mitigations: (1) downgrade max_batch_size to 16, (2) pin model to exact version, (3) upgrade SDK to 1.4.2 and report.

Olivia (Platform): Longer-term we should add strict dim-check in the batching layer and drop mixed batches before kernel execution with a clear 400 error message. I can schedule a canary.

Maya (ML Eng): Agreed. Also we can add an assert in the coalescer that checks `embedding_dim` metadata for all items in batch and refuses to merge mismatched items. That will trade off some batching efficiency but avoid silent failures.

Jordan (SRE): I captured a worker log snippet during my local repro: 
```
2024-11-03T14:21:58Z batch_coalescer INFO Batch composed: id=0x7f size=64 models=[text-embed-uni-1536,text-embed-uni-1536,text-embed-mini-128,...]
2024-11-03T14:21:58Z batch_executor ERROR EmbeddingOp failed: InvalidEmbeddingDimension expected=1536 actual=128 stack=/src/...
2024-11-03T14:21:58Z worker WARN Dropping 12 requests from batch id=0x7f due to dim mismatch
```
That last line is concerning — worker dropped some requests but still attempted op. Need safer fail-fast.

Olivia (Platform): I'll open a platform ticket for `strict-batch-dim-check` and propose a canary flag `BATCH_STRICT_DIM_CHECK=true` for the next runtime build. Can someone volunteer to own the rollout?

Jordan (SRE): I can own the canary. I'll prepare CI job, run on two nodes for 24h and monitor p99 and error rates.

deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime-v3.6.1-canary -> embed-worker-[canary-02,canary-03]

Maya (ML Eng): Also we should improve error message to include `expected_dim` and `received_dim` plus `model` names to make support/customer triage faster.

Riley (Support): For ACME I recommended: 1) set `max_batch_size` to 16, 2) pin model version, 3) upgrade SDK to 1.4.2, 4) send us a trace_id if it happens again. They said they'll try the mitigations and report back in 2 hours.

Riley (Support): If the canary shows positive signal Jordan, we'll follow up with a patch and release notes so customers know to upgrade. :thumbsup:

Jordan (SRE): Will post canary metrics in #eng-sre in 2h.

Maya (ML Eng): Thanks — also adding a tiny repro snippet for support playbook to share with customers: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('KEY'))
# avoid mixing model variants when using high concurrency
resp = c.embeddings.create(model='text-embed-uni-1536', input=['a','b','c'], max_batch_size=16)
```

Riley (Support): Logged customer case RED-4721 and marked high priority. Will update thread with ACME feedback.

ops-bot: Note: set alert threshold lowered for route=/v1/embeddings to p99 1.0s until mitigations are confirmed.

Riley (Support): Closing loop for now — will reopen if ACME sees failures after the mitigation steps.

Jordan (SRE): Thanks team — follow-ups: (1) canary rollout, (2) add strict-dim-check ticket, (3) support playbook update.

Maya (ML Eng): I'll draft the PR for the assert in the coalescer and include unit tests.

Riley (Support): Marking done for customer-facing next steps.
